title: Vector solitons in nonlinear lattices with competing SPM and XPM terms
authors: Liangwei Zeng, Boris A. Malomed, Dumitru Mihalache, Xing Zhu
abstract: We demonstrate that two-component photonic nonlinear lattices with opposite signs of the out-of-phase spatially modulated SPM and XPM coefficients can support two types of optical vector solitons (VSs), the fundamental and mixed ones. The fundamental VSs are composed of two Gaussian-like components, while the mixed ones combine Gaussian-like and dipole components. The structures and stability of both types of the VSs are investigated. The VSs are stable, except for narrow intervals at small values of the propagation constant.
summary: This paper theoretically investigates vector solitons in nonlinear photonic lattices where competing nonlinear effects (SPM and XPM) are present. Using coupled NLSEs, the authors demonstrate the existence of stable fundamental and mixed soliton types. The stability is rigorously analyzed using linear stability theory, mapping out the parameter space where these robust light structures can propagate.
main_problem: The study investigates the existence and stability of two-component optical vector solitons (VSs) propagating in nonlinear photonic lattices characterized by competing Self-Phase Modulation (SPM) and Cross-Phase Modulation (XPM) terms.
main_result: The research confirms that stable fundamental and mixed vector solitons exist in these lattices, except for narrow ranges of the propagation constant. The stability analysis maps out the parameter space where these localized structures persist.
method: The authors employed a combination of analytical techniques (solving stationary equations) and rigorous numerical methods, including linear stability analysis via eigenvalue problems and direct simulation of perturbed propagation.
model_or_system: The system is modeled by coupled Nonlinear Schrödinger Equations (NLSEs) describing two-component light propagation in a nonlinear lattice defined by spatially-modulated coefficients. The competition between SPM and XPM terms is key to the physics.
key_observables: Profiles of the two components ($U_1, U_2$), total power ($P_1, P_2$), amplitudes ($A_1, A_2$), and the real part of the eigenvalues ($	ext{Re}(\lambda)$) used to determine stability.
important_parameters: The nonlinear coupling strength ($\gamma$), the propagation constants ($b_1, b_2$), and the spatial modulation parameters are crucial for defining the soliton types and stability regimes.
main_assumptions: Stability analysis relies on linearizing the equations around the stationary solution, and some initial approximations treat the XPM term as a small perturbation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the profiles and stability regions for fundamental and mixed VSs, mapping out critical values ($b_{2cr}$) that determine the stability domain based on the propagation constants.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the physical model and stationary solutions, followed by a detailed stability analysis using eigenvalue solvers. The results are then systematically presented by comparing the characteristics and stability of the two distinct soliton types (fundamental and mixed) across varying parameters.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to quantum optics and nonlinear photonics, as vector solitons represent robust, localized energy packets whose stability is governed by complex nonlinear interactions, mirroring phenomena studied in quantum light-matter interactions.
